sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Henderson County, NC?
sections.html:
Deeds for Henderson County property are recorded at the Register of Deeds in the county courthouse at 200 North Grove Street in Hendersonville. The office records documents Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and the main line is 828-697-4901.

The office describes itself as a recording office. Its staff check that a document meets North Carolina recording standards, but they cannot give legal advice, so questions about how to word a deed belong with a real estate attorney or your closing attorney. Payment can be made by check, cash, money order, or credit or debit card, and a card payment carries a processing fee charged by the card vendor rather than by the county.

The Census Bureau lists 372.95 square miles of land in the county and about 311.8 residents per square mile for 2020, a spread that produces everything from small town lots to larger tracts in the recorded deeds. The county's Land Records section sits in the same courthouse and keeps the tax listing index in step with what the register records.

sections.h2: What does the Henderson County Register of Deeds keep on file?
sections.html:
The office keeps the permanent public record of land ownership in the county. Its own list of holdings includes:

  • Land transfers, easements, rights of way and surveys
  • Security instruments such as deeds of trust, mortgages and UCC filings
  • Separation agreements
  • Birth, death and marriage certificates, with certified copies at $10.00 each and photocopies at $.25
  • Assumed business name (DBA) filings and notary oaths
  • Military records, which are recorded and certified for the veteran at no charge

Marriage licenses are issued by appointment only, between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM on weekdays. Appointments are set by phone, not by email. Marriage and vital record work shares the office with recording, so call ahead before bringing a deed package during a busy stretch.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Henderson County?
sections.html:
Fees follow the uniform schedule in North Carolina G.S. 161-10, so the base charges match every other county. A general instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages, and a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages.

Recording fees set by G.S. 161-10 and charged by the Henderson County Register of Deeds
ItemFee as printed in the statute
Instrument in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, then $4.00 per added page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added
Extra instrument in one document$10.00 each

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Source: G.S. 161-10. Ask the Henderson County office for any added charge for services such as vital record requests.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax when a Henderson County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. North Carolina law makes the transferor pay the tax to the register of deeds before the deed can be recorded.

The rate printed in G.S. 105-228.30 is one dollar on each five hundred dollars, or fractional part, of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed. Half of the collected amount stays with the county general fund and the rest goes to the state. Your closing attorney normally pays it from your proceeds and hands the receipt to the register of deeds with the deed.

Because the tax is tied to the price on the deed, ask the closing attorney for the figure on your settlement statement instead of working it from memory. The statute is at G.S. 105-228.30.

sections.h2: How do I search Henderson County deeds and plats online?
sections.html:
The county posts an online deed index covering 1979 to the present, hosted through a records vendor. You acknowledge a disclaimer first, and the page recommends a desktop or laptop with Chrome or Edge, cookies on and pop-ups allowed.

Plats have their own search path. In the Register of Deeds system, choose View Images, set the book type to Plat, and enter either the year the plat was recorded or Cabinet A, B or C as the book. The page number is the plat or slide number. The county's guide shows recent years running in sequence, with 2025 plats on slides 16021 to 16768 and 2026 starting at 16769.

A privacy rule is printed on the search page: under G.S. 132-1.8, a document filed for recording should not carry Social Security, driver license, bank account or card numbers unless the law requires them. A person can ask the register in writing to remove such a number from an online image, and no fee is charged for that redaction.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter on a Henderson County sale?
sections.html:
A deed protects the buyer against later claims from the moment it is registered in the county where the land lies. G.S. 47-18 says conveyances, options, leases over three years and similar rights are not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until registered, and priority follows the time of registration.

For a seller, that means a deed left unrecorded leaves the buyer exposed until it is filed. If you hold a house through an older deed that was never registered, ask your attorney to record it before you list. See G.S. 47-18.

  • Confirm the deed shows the drafter's name or firm and meets the page, margin and type standards in G.S. 161-14.
  • Have the parcel identification number and a tax statement ready for the closing attorney.
  • Ask that any old deed of trust be satisfied of record; satisfactions carry no recording fee.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Henderson County homes?
sections.html:
Henderson County is a higher-value, older-skewing market. QuickFacts estimates 122,375 residents in July 2025, up 5.2 percent from the April 2020 base, and 61,173 housing units.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024: $351,400
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 75.0 percent
  • Median gross rent: $1,187
  • Median household income: $68,187
  • Residents aged 65 and over: 29.1 percent
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,093

Nearly three in ten residents are 65 or older, and the county tax pages carry relief programs aimed at that group, covered in the last section below.

sections.h2: What property tax steps come with selling a house in Henderson County?
sections.html:
The county Tax Department handles assessment and collection separately from the Register of Deeds. It lists roughly 71,500 parcels, and its real property appraisers are certified by the North Carolina Department of Revenue.

The county is preparing for its 2027 reappraisal and its Tax Department invites residents to information sessions on how values are set. North Carolina counties must reappraise real property at least every eight years as of January 1. Taxes are due September 1 and become delinquent with interest after January 5, according to G.S. 105-360, so a fall or winter closing needs a clear plan for who pays the current bill.

Seniors and disabled owners may qualify for the elderly or disabled exclusion, set at the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800. Disabled veterans may exclude the first $45,000 of value. Applications go to the county assessor on the state form, not to the Register of Deeds. See the G.S. 105-277.1 text and the county's Tax Department page.

faqs.q: Does the Henderson County Register of Deeds charge a county fee to record a deed?
faqs.a: The recording fees are the uniform amounts in G.S. 161-10: $26.00 for the first 15 pages of a general instrument and $4.00 for each added page. Card payments add a vendor processing fee that the county does not keep. Ask the office at 828-697-4901 for any service charge outside recording.

faqs.q: Can I pay by card at the Henderson County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts credit and debit cards along with checks, cash and money orders. A processing fee is charged by the card vendor, not by Henderson County. The office also says it is a recording office, so it will not review the legal content of a deed for you.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Henderson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 requires the transferor to pay the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at one dollar per five hundred dollars of value or part of that amount.

faqs.q: Where can I find an old Henderson County plat?
faqs.a: Use the online Register of Deeds system, choose View Images, set the book type to Plat, and enter the recording year or Cabinet A, B or C as the book. The plat or slide number goes in the page field. Leading zeros are not needed.

faqs.q: What if my Henderson County deed has a mistake after recording?
faqs.a: Contact the closing attorney or the lawyer who drafted it right away. The register's staff can show you what the record contains, but they state that they cannot advise anyone in a legal capacity, so the fix has to come from your attorney.
